name: Itzamna

domain_history.domain: creator/high-god figure, "Lord of the Heavens and Earth," associated with writing, divination, and the invention of the calendar; depicted as an aged man ("God D" in the Schellhas system)

notes: Attested from the Preclassic period through the Postclassic (Classic-period scribal glyphs, Itzamnaaj, and Postclassic Yucatec sources, Itzamná/Zamná both attested) — genuine documented longevity/continuity across the full span, unlike Kukulkan (see below), whose attestation is regionally and temporally narrower. Karl Taube: "Itzamná is probably the most important Classic Maya deity, yet he remains one of the most poorly understood" (likely from Taube, The Major Gods of Ancient Yucatan, Dumbarton Oaks, 1992 — exact publication not directly confirmed in this research pass). Iconographically described as an aged form of the Maize God.
